fieldNotes.truckGate: ROSTER COORDINATE CORRECTION: the supplied coords landed on the Killingly Commons retail shopping center, not the plant. The real Frito-Lay Killingly plant is at 1886 Upper Maple St, ~2.3 km NW (center ~41.8605, -71.8905). A single access road off Upper Maple St crosses the New England Central rail line at a grade crossing and runs into the secured plant property; the truck entrance is a controlled gate on this access road. The wooded approach obscures the exact gate from satellite and Street View - medium confidence, flagged.
fieldNotes.guardShack: A guard booth is likely at this 700-employee plant given the single controlled access road, but it could not be visually confirmed - the entrance road runs under heavy tree canopy. Marked true at medium confidence and flagged.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Large internal paved aprons and trailer yards between the gate and the dock banks - ample inside holding room.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: Long wooded access road from Upper Maple St plus expansive internal yard - holds well over 3 trucks.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: The wooded entrance road is constrained; unclear whether there is room to add an express lane - flagged, left false.
fieldNotes.entryExitTogether: Single access road serves both in and out.
fieldNotes.entryLanes: Estimated 1 inbound - low confidence, entrance obscured by tree canopy.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Long dock banks on multiple building faces (north face and east/SE faces) with many trailers backed in. Total estimated ~50 - 50+ band.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Very extensive trailer drop yards on the north (paved) and south/SW (gravel overflow lot) - hundreds of trailers in long rows, far exceeding 50 stalls.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Dock banks on physically distinct building faces (north face and east/SE faces) indicating separate shipping/receiving clusters.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Located in the small town of Dayville (Killingly), CT, surrounded by woods, lakes/ponds, and a quarry; small-town/rural industrial setting - Rural.
fieldNotes.multipleFacilities: Single large connected plant building mass with attached process structures - not a multi-cluster campus.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale clearly identifiable - low confidence.
fieldNotes.railServed: Confirmed - the New England Central rail line runs along the west side of the property; the plant access road crosses it at a grade crossing and a spur appears to serve the site.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter box yields ~90 acres including the plant building and the north and south drop yards.
fieldNotes.trailersVisible: ~350 trailers counted across the north paved yard, south gravel yard, and dock faces - approximate.
fieldNotes.dockDoorCount: Overhead estimate; dock faces partially obscured by backed-in trailers - moderate confidence.
